rows.note: Use this as the everyday noun for buying now and paying later, rather than for praise or academic credit.

example.english: This shop is willing to give regular customers credit.
example.traditional: 呢間舖頭肯畀熟客賒數。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 tau4 hang2 bei2 suk6 haak3 se1 sou3

rows.note: Use this for a course credit or credit counted toward graduation.

example.english: This course gives me credit toward my graduation requirements.
example.traditional: 呢科有三個學分，畀我計入畢業要求。
example.jyutping: ni1 fo1 jau5 saam1 go3 hok6 fan1 bei2 ngo5 gai3 jap6 bat1 jip6 jiu1 kau4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for recognition and admiration of someone's actions.

example.english: They deserve credit from everyone for doing so many good deeds.
example.traditional: 佢做咗咁多好事，值得大家畀佢讚賞。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zou6 zo2 gam3 do1 hou2 si6 zik6 dak1 daai6 gaa1 bei2 keoi5 zaan3 soeng2

rows.note: In a film or TV context, use this for the names and information shown in the credit sequence, not ordinary dialogue subtitles.

example.english: The credit sequence at the end of the film lists all the crew members' names.
example.traditional: 套戲尾段嘅字幕列晒幕後工作人員個名。
example.jyutping: tou3 hei3 mei5 dyun6 ge3 zi6 mok6 lit6 saai3 mok6 hau6 gung1 zok3 jan4 jyun4 go3 meng2
